title: Video factory
summary: Four agents make a short film: a director plans, a Blender artist builds and renders the scene headless, a Hyperframes compositor composes and exports it, and a viewer judges the exported film. CPU-only; no paid media services.
lineage: Redesigned from OpenRig's earlier Blender and Hyperframes studio rigs (openrig-studio lineage); not an export of any live rig.
built_by: the rigs-to-builder packaging environment (native bundles stamp sourceHost "rigs-to-builder")
models_test_label: TEST — cheap smoke-test models; the recommended configuration is the default

rigs.name: video-factory
rigs.summary: A small video factory: a director turns a brief into a shot plan, a Blender artist builds and renders the scene headless, a Hyperframes compositor puts it into an HTML/CSS/GSAP composition and exports the film, and a viewer judges the exported film against the plan. CPU-only; no paid media generation. Recommended models.

members.label: Director — holds the brief, the plan and the final report
Blender artist — builds and renders the scene
Hyperframes compositor — owns the timeline and the exported film
Viewer — watches the exported film and judges it against the plan

prerequisites.name: Node.js
prerequisites.why: runs the launcher and npx for the pinned Hyperframes CLI

prerequisites.name: Blender
prerequisites.why: the Blender artist renders the scene headless (Cycles, CPU); must be on PATH as `blender`

prerequisites.name: Chrome or Chromium
check: command -v google-chrome || command -v chromium || command -v chromium-browser
prerequisites.why: Hyperframes renders the HTML composition in a headless browser

prerequisites.name: Network access to npm
prerequisites.why: fetches the pinned Hyperframes CLI (and, at render time, the pinned GSAP script from jsDelivr)

prerequisites.name: Claude Code
prerequisites.why: runtime for the director and viewer; your login, never packaged

prerequisites.name: Codex
prerequisites.why: runtime for the Blender artist and compositor; your login, never packaged

permissions.effect: Keeps the Codex sandbox ON (no general network). A Codex seat can write in the project and the system's temporary folders. OpenRig also lists one more folder in the seat's sandbox policy, <OpenRig shared-docs root>/rigs/<rig>/state/<pod>, but does not create it and this factory does not use it; writes there fail unless something else has created it. Exactly two commands run outside the sandbox without a prompt, and only as STANDALONE commands, one per call: `rig …` and `npx --yes hyperframes@0.6.20 …`. A chained or cd-prefixed line runs inside the sandbox and fails. Blender, ffmpeg and ffprobe stay inside the sandbox. Codex loads these only for a trusted project; launching with OpenRig registers that trust.
permissions.tested: video-factory 0.1.3 and 0.1.4 package proofs from the download (OpenRig 0.6.1, Codex 0.159, 2026-09-29): standalone rig queue calls handed work on, blender rendered inside the sandbox, standalone npx --yes hyperframes@0.6.20 ran under the rule; chained rig/npx lines were measured to fail. Evidence: video/evidence/03-package-proof-0.1.3/ and 04-package-proof-0.1.4/

permissions.effect: Pre-approves only `rig`, `ffprobe`, `ffmpeg`, `mkdir`, `ls`, and two exact commands: `bash .claude/skills/film-review/scripts/review.sh` (the viewer's review) and `node tools/check-delivery.mjs` (the delivery gate: it hashes the film, stamps the viewer's verdict and checks it; plain Node, it reads the project and writes only review/VERDICT.md). No general shell; anything else asks as usual.

first_job: rig send studio-director@video-factory "Read BRIEF.md and run the production as PRODUCTION-GUIDE.md describes."
expected_output: PLAN.md whose first line cites 'Recipe: S… (video-factory-craft/shot-library.md)'
setup_prompt:
Set up Video factory 0.1.5, an OpenRig factory from rigs.to.

1. Download the archive and check its hash before unpacking. The sha256 must be exactly ff1f89eab9bc62c0a555c57a47dfcb546d2575bc32dd00eba1844f9d4b43795f:
   curl -fLO https://github.com/mvschwarz/rigs-to-apps/releases/download/video-factory-v0.1.5/video-factory-0.1.5.tar.gz
   echo "ff1f89eab9bc62c0a555c57a47dfcb546d2575bc32dd00eba1844f9d4b43795f  video-factory-0.1.5.tar.gz" | shasum -a 256 -c
2. Unpack it somewhere stable and read SETUP.md inside before running anything:
   mkdir -p ~/rig-factories && tar -xzf video-factory-0.1.5.tar.gz -C ~/rig-factories
   cd ~/rig-factories/video-factory-0.1.5
3. Follow SETUP.md with the OpenRig I already run (leave my other rigs and its kernel alone): run
   node launch.mjs --project <dir> --plan-only, explain to me every permission change it prints, and launch only
   after I agree. Never pipe anything into a shell.
